subject: gk
question: Babur ruled over Delhi till ________ year.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1530**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Babur**

 
 
• At the age of twelve, Babur faced revolt as he succeeded to the throne of Fergana in Akhsikent.
 
• Two years later, he took Samarkand, only to lose Fergana not long after.
 
• In his attempt to reconquer Fergana, he lost control of Samarkand.
 
• Babur was compelled to abdicate his kingdom following the Uzbeg invasion, another Mongol tribe.
 
• At the age of 22, he eventually conquered Kabul in 1504 after years of traveling.
 
• Later, in the year 1526, he took Delhi and Agra after defeating Ibrahim Lodi, in the renowned battle of Panipat. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**** Some Important Mughal Emperor**

 
 

 Mughal Emperor
 Reign
 Key Achievements
 Significant Events
 
 
 
 

 Babur
 1526-1530
 Established Mughal Empire in India after defeating Ibrahim Lodi in the Battle of Panipat
 Captured Gwalior, Chanderi, and Dholpur; implemented administrative reforms; wrote the Baburnama
 
 

 Humayun
 1530-1540; 1555-1556
 Reclaimed the Mughal throne after a period of exile; expanded the empire to Gujarat and Bengal
 Defeated by Sher Shah Suri and forced into exile; died after falling down a flight of stairs
 
 

 Akbar
 1556-1605
 Established a strong central government; promoted religious tolerance and cultural synthesis; expanded the empire to include most of northern and central India
 Instituted the Mansabdari system; married a Rajput princess; built the city of Fatehpur Sikri
 
 

 Jahangir
 1605-1627
 Consolidated Mughal power in northern India; patronized the arts and architecture; allowed the English East India Company to establish a trading post in Surat
 Married Nur Jahan, who played an active role in the administration; ordered the execution of his rebellious son Khusrau
 
 

 Shah Jahan
 1628-1658
 Commissioned the construction of the Taj Mahal and other iconic monuments; expanded the empire to include parts of southern India; implemented various social and economic reforms
 Faced a rebellion by his son Aurangzeb; was deposed and imprisoned in the Red Fort
 
 

 Aurangzeb
 1658-1707
 Expanded the empire to include the Deccan and parts of central India; implemented strict Islamic laws and policies; faced rebellions from various quarters
 Imprisoned his father Shah Jahan; executed his brother Dara Shikoh; faced a protracted war with the Maratha Confederacy
 
 

 Bahadur Shah Zafar
 1837-1857
 Last Mughal Emperor; faced the Indian Rebellion of 1857; exiled to Burma by the British
 Played a largely symbolic role; patronized poets and artists; wrote several poems and ghazals
